title.narrative: Situational Analysis of Myanmar’s Higher Education (HE) and TVET Sectors

description.narrative:
The funds from the 42 C/5 regular budget for PAX/UN (2024–2025) were dedicated to supporting the UNESCO Antenna Office in Yangon in advancing actions related to crisis preparedness, response, and early recovery. Within this framework, the Situation Analysis on the Impact of Conflict on Youth’s Educational Experiences in Myanmar was conducted from February to September 2025.
The overarching objective of this study is to provide an understanding of how the political crisis in Myanmar has disrupted tertiary education, particularly among marginalised groups, and to identify barriers and coping strategies that can guide future policy and development interventions, aimed at improving access to education, ensuring quality, and supporting the psychosocial well-being of youth during periods of conflict and instability.
The study provides evidence on how ongoing political instability and its consequences have affected tertiary education participation, institutional capacity, and labour market outcomes. Furthermore, the study examines the emergence of alternative education pathways, as well as the coping and resilience strategies adopted by youth, education providers, and stakeholders in response to these challenges. Primary data collection involved students, professionals, and ministry officials engaged in higher education (HE) and technical and vocational education and training (TVET), as well as representatives from business and industry in Myanmar.
